_README: Executable half of .claude/DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md. The markdown holds the
narrative; this holds the one thing prose cannot do — answer 'is it still
broken?' by being RUN.
WHY: on 2026-08-12 the tracker said DQ-54 was 'Open — report-only' when it
had been fixed and merged that morning, and its own row said 'three call
sites' when there were nine. Its header said Last Updated 2026-08-08. A
hand-written status decays silently, and this repo has the receipts: #398
hid for ten weeks, DQ-54's prose recurred in four days.
THE RATCHET RUNS BOTH WAYS — that is the whole point:
declared 'fixed' + check FAILS  -> red. A regression, or a fix that never was.
declared 'open'  + check PASSES -> red. Silently fixed; the ledger is lying
the other way and nobody would ever look.
Only the second direction catches the failure mode that actually hurt here.
COVERAGE: every DQ id in the markdown must appear here. A new row without an
entry fails the coverage test, so the ledger cannot grow un-checkable rows.
Same shape as scripts/check_test_quarantine.py, which already works this way.
check: null is HONEST, not a TODO to hide behind. It means nobody has written
a falsifiable check yet, and the count of nulls is reported on every run so
the gap stays visible. An invented check that cannot fail is what produced
DQ-30's '0% drift' verification — worse than no check.

DQ-25.fixed_by: STALE, closed 2026-08-14 on measurement. The row said sepp_structured_requirements was EMPTY for the Transport & Infrastructure SEPP. It is not: joining sepp_structured_requirements.provision_id -> regulatory_provisions.document_id gives 110 rows for that SEPP (69 + 41 across its two document rows), the largest holding after Exempt and Complying Development. 553 of the table's 560 rows carry a NULL sepp_name, which is why a naive `GROUP BY sepp_name` shows nothing for Transport and made the row look true - the SEPP is recoverable through provision_id, not from that column. Nothing was built to close this; it had already stopped being true and no check existed to notice.
DQ-25.why_no_check: Closed on measurement, and a standing probe would guard the wrong thing. The row's claim was 'this table is empty for this SEPP'; it holds 110 rows, so there is nothing left to watch that is specific to Transport. The real residual - 553 of 560 rows carrying a NULL sepp_name, so the owning SEPP is only recoverable through provision_id - is a different defect about that column and belongs in its own row if anyone wants it guarded.

DQ-70.note: 595 -> 262 on 2026-08-15, and the 333 that came off were NOT re-extracted - they were never stale. THE RE-EXPORT OPTIMISATION WAS DEFEATING ITSELF. Every re-export therefore created a permanent false entry, clearable only by the full re-extraction the branch exists to avoid. MEASURED BEFORE ACTING, via scripts/dq70_measure_text_delta.py, which compares the extracted-from version against the currently-held version in R2 using the existing pdf_text_hash detector: 1 chapter re-export only (ashfield/chapter-e1-heritage, 333 served, 25,959,773 bytes recompressed to 3,879,460 with byte-identical normalised text), 8 chapters real text change (262 served), 0 unknown. THE REMAINING 262 ARE GENUINE and still need re-extraction: city_of_sydney section-3 (92), leichhardt part-e water (43), hornsby part3-residential (32), georges_river part-3 (26), ku_ring_gai section-c-part-24 (25), section-a-part-4 (18), section-a-part-9 (18), section-c-part-23 (8). DQ-76.passes_when: exit 0 - no served provision carries PDF-extraction residue (TeX control sequence, non-money $, or a brace group wrapping a single symbol)

DQ-76.note: REPAIRED 2026-08-15: 104 -> 9 by scripts/repair_tex_residue.py, verified by the probe rather than asserted. THE METRIC WAS WRONG TWICE FIRST, and both corrections are the point of this row. (1) It listed five TeX macros I had seen, counting 10 while reporting CLEAN on 89 rows with the identical fault - a row carrying only \dag,  ullet, \div or \lambda scored green. (2) After widening, its brace class [-A-Za-z0-9] could not see an EMPTY '{}', nor '{ : }', nor '{ t h }', so the first repair pass drove the count to 0 while 103 rows still carried braces. It is now ANY brace, checked by sampling all 103 - none legitimate. THE REPAIR'S ONE RULE: no digit may change. It strips TeX wrappers and keeps contents; it never joins split digits, so '12 00 { m } 2' became '12 00 m 2' and NOT '1,200 m2', however obvious that reading is - that is a judgement about the source PDF, not a regex. Machine-checked per row: the ordered digit sequence must be identical or the row is skipped. 0 rows were skipped; 19,957 served rows before and after. THE RESIDUAL 9 ARE NOT REPAIRABLE THIS WAY. Each is a LONE brace substituting for another character rather than wrapping one: 7 HTML table cells reading '200m{-300m2' where '{' replaced a '2' (the neighbouring cells read '>300m2-900m2' and '600m2-900m2', which is why the reading is obvious and still a guess), plus 81108 '(ground or upper floor}' and 81112 '{incised decorative patterns' where a brace replaced a parenthesis. Deciding which character a lone brace should be requires the source document. SEPARATE AND LARGER, not counted here: 244 served rows carry '900 m m' where the source reads 900mm, and ~165 carry letter-spacing like 'F o o d A c t 2003'. Stripping the '$' from '$F o o d A c t 2003' removed the symptom this metric could see and left that corruption invisible - a repair blinding a metric, which needs its own row.

But the rows just inside the boundary carry REAL CONTROLS with map text interleaved: id 95870 (0.230) reads 'Objectives (a) Ensure that the safety and amenity of pedestrians and cyclists is not compromised by off-street parking access points'; id 95375 (0.202) reads 'This locality is bounded by Ashmore Street to the north, Mitchell Road to the east'; id 95887 (0.213) reads 'Building heights are to comply with Figure 6.1'. The remedy is to strip the figure text from the provision at EXTRACTION, keeping the prose, not to drop the row and not to edit the text with a regex: separating interleaved map labels from a control needs the source PDF's layout, which is exactly the information the extractor threw away. The metric stays as it is and stays RED at 111. It correctly identifies affected rows; what it cannot do is tell a pure-figure row from a mixed one, and that distinction is the whole remedy. Thresholds were read off the distribution (>=0.50: 34, >=0.30: 83, >=0.20: 128, >=0.10: 663) and the >=100-token floor separates this from DQ-77 by dropping the 31-token 's o o m m' rows. 110 of 111 are one council's Section 2 precinct pages, which is the shape of one broken document rather than a threshold artefact.

DQ-79.passes_when: exit 0 - every active chapter's recorded content is large enough to be the document
DQ-79.red_when: a chapter's stored url_content_length is too small to be the document, which means the monitor recorded the size of something other than the file - a range response, an error page, or a truncated fetch
DQ-79.note: FIXED 2026-08-15: 1 -> 0. BUT MY FIRST DIAGNOSIS OF THIS ROW WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT. I claimed the stored hash was 'a hash of the failure' and that hornsby's document could no longer be fetched, and I therefore claimed DQ-70 overstated by 32. ALL OF THAT IS RETRACTED. The user supplied the council's current URL; fetching it, then the stored one, then comparing against the registry showed the document is fine (14,117,244 bytes) and the stored content_hash 193ac6a4... is a BYTE-EXACT match for the live file, ETag included. So hornsby's source genuinely DID change (Last-Modified 25 June 2026, extracted 9 May 2026) and DQ-70's 595 is CORRECT. THE REAL BUG was narrower and entirely in one field. head_request() falls back to 'GET Range: bytes=0-0' when a server answers HEAD with 405, then stored THAT response's Content-Length - which is 1, because we asked for one byte. The document's real size sits in Content-Range: bytes 0-0/14117244. Fixed by reading the total, with a fallback to plain Content-Length so a server that ignores Range behaves as before. WHY IT SURVIVED: url_content_length is not used to decide whether content changed - ETag and hash are - so a wrong value corrupted a recorded number rather than a decision, and nothing failed. The row was corrected with the VERIFIED length, and content_hash was deliberately left alone: rewriting a hash confirmed correct against the live file is the shortcut this row's own note warns against. council_url repointed from the v/2 path to the council's current v/3 dated filename - both serve byte-identical content, so that is tidiness, not repair. MY 403 ON THE FIRST FETCH was self-inflicted: I sent a browser User-Agent. The monitor's own UA is allowed. That is the REVERSE of the pattern recorded in memory ('council sites 403 automated fetchers, a real browser passes') and is worth knowing for hornsby specifically.
